hook.line: People are now asking ChatGPT to take a selfie of itself, and it's breaking the internet.
hook.visual: Creator cut out in the bottom right over a ChatGPT screenshot showing the blurry 'selfie' result, with a white title box 'ChatGPT just took a selfie of itself' and an emoji.

beats.what: Result first: the strange selfie ChatGPT made fills the background behind the creator, under a boxed title.
Cut to the ChatGPT 'Create image' screen with '/image' typed: step one of how to do it.
The full prompt text appears as a card behind him.
Back to the blurry selfie result as he describes it.
Variation: a cat's face as someone else's ChatGPT selfie.
Variation: a robot with a glowing smiley face.
Cut to the creator alone in his room with a boxed title 'Follow and comment Selfie and I'll send it', pointing at the camera.

why_it_works: Result shown in the first frame, so the viewer stays to learn how to get their own.
Fast speech (5 words/s) and a background change every ~2.7 s fit the whole trend into 22 s.
Different results (cat, robot) turn it into 'what will mine be?', a personal curiosity gap.
Comment-keyword CTA for the prompt drives comments (25.3k) and follows.
weaknesses: Single-word captions sit right over his face and chest; most text is outside the safe area (0.933).
The prompt is shown on screen at 7 s, so the 'comment to get it' ask is partly redundant.
for_robert: Put the payoff image behind him in the first frame and make the comment keyword the CTA; Fred could hold up a sign with the keyword at the end.
